vars.team_intro: For significant features or changes that are more than a few lines of code, run a structured multi-agent workflow. You are the lead: start each role with `spawn_agent`, using the type, `model_config_id` and `reasoning_effort` from the role roster below. In its prompt, tell the child it is not the lead and to call `read_skill` with its role skill first, then give it the task as a complete prompt, because a child starts with no history of this chat. Use `wait_agent` to finish a step before starting the next. Only you can spawn roles: a child cannot spawn another and cannot ask the human, so relay its questions in this chat.
vars.worktree_section:
**All agents share one workspace dir.** Before starting any agent, run `team-guard workspace new <feature>`, then `team-guard workspace attach <repo-path>` from the workspace dir for each repo the feature touches. Each attached worktree is on the same branch name in its repo. Every spawned agent shares this chat's workspace machine, so give each one the absolute workspace path in its prompt; each agent edits code inside `repos/<repo>/`, and the workflow artifacts stay in the workspace dir.

**Where work lives.** Only `~/work` (`/home/coder/work`) survives a workspace stop; everything else under the home directory, such as `~/skim`, is erased whenever the workspace stops. Clone every repo into `~/work`. The image sets `TEAM_WORKSPACE_ROOT` to `~/work/.agentic-workflow/work` and `TEAM_ARCHIVE_ROOT` to `~/work/.agentic-workflow/archive`, so workspaces and archives persist: use the workspace path that `team-guard` prints, not `~/.agentic-workflow`. After the first commit on a branch, push it and open a draft PR with `gh pr create --draft`, linking the issue if there is one. Then push after every commit, so no work exists only in the workspace. Exception: before pushing a security fix, or work on a vulnerability the security review finds, check the repo's visibility with `gh repo view <owner/name> --json visibility`. If it isn't PRIVATE (public, internal, or the check fails), treat it as public. Public: never push it. Commit it on a local branch under ~/work and stop for the human. If the security review finds a vulnerability after the branch is pushed, stop pushing, keep the details only in the workspace (never in the PR, commit messages or chat-visible links), and tell the human in the chat. Private: the normal draft-PR flow applies, but don't describe the vulnerability in the PR title or description beyond what's needed, and tell the human in the chat.
vars.role_files: Role definitions are the skills `role-<role>` in `~/.coder/skills/`, which a spawned child reads with `read_skill`. Coder keeps the first skill of each name it finds and scans `~/.coder` before the project, so a project cannot override a role, and a project skill with the same name as one of ours (such as `tdd` or `grilling`) is silently dropped. Give project skills other names.
vars.child_guard: **If you were told to read a `role-*` skill, you are that role and not the lead.** Follow that skill and the task you were given. Do not start agents, run `team-guard workspace new`, propose a variant or ask the human anything; the sections below are for the lead. Return your report as your final message.
vars.design_review: Post the doc in the chat so the human can read it there, and wait. The architect revises from the human's comments in the chat. The human approves by replying `approve design` in the chat.
vars.human_gate: Draft the PR description and put it on the draft PR with `gh pr edit --body-file <file>`, then ask the human to review the draft PR (the description and the full diff, test changes included). Mark it ready only after they approve.
vars.ship: The draft PR already exists and every commit is pushed (see Where work lives). After the human approves, run `gh pr ready`. You cannot merge: branch rulesets leave that to the human. `team-guard sign` skips signing here (`TEAM_SANDBOX=1`) and the commits stay unsigned: say so in the PR description.
vars.review_stop: the review of the draft PR before you mark it ready
vars.first_push: The first push opens the draft PR and needs no approval; marking it ready does. Push after every commit (a security fix on a public repo is never pushed; see Where work lives), and sign a fix
vars.security_stop: A security fix, or a vulnerability in existing code that the security review finds, follows the rule in Where work lives: on a public repo it is never pushed and the details stay in the workspace; on a private repo the draft-PR flow applies without describing the vulnerability. Either way, tell the human in the chat.
